version.changelog:
- Removed the file references/details.md.
- No other changes to documentation or functionality in this release.

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent with being a runtime security plugin: its install and runtime instructions match the claimed purpose, but it relies on an external 'Core' service (which will receive content for analysis) and the SKILL.md/registry metadata contain small mismatches you should verify before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name, description and runtime instructions align: the skill tells the agent to install an OpenClaw plugin package and restart the gateway, and describes detection being performed by a remote 'Core' service. The actions requested (install plugin, restart, read sample file) are coherent with a security plugin purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions direct the agent to install a plugin and restart the gateway (expected for a plugin). They also instruct the agent to read a local sample file to demonstrate detection. Importantly, the SKILL.md states that 'All security detection is performed by Core'—which implies that file contents and other inspected data will be sent to an external service for analysis. That behavior is consistent with the described feature set but is a privacy/telemetry consideration the user should understand and accept.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill (no install spec or code included). The SKILL.md tells the user to run 'openclaw plugins install @openguardrails/moltguard' — a reasonable install step for an OpenClaw plugin. However the registry metadata shows no homepage while the SKILL.md references a GitHub repo; that mismatch means you should verify the package origin (package namespace vs GitHub repository) before running the install command.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request environment variables in the registry metadata, but it documents auto-registration with Core and storing credentials at ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard. That is proportional for a cloud-backed detection service, but it does mean credentials and potentially inspected content will be persisted locally and transmitted to the Core service—confirm you accept sharing that data and the storage location.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not force-installed (always: false) and does not request special platform privileges in the metadata. It does instruct installing a plugin that will persist on disk and create credentials under the user's home directory, which is normal for a plugin but worth noting.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing: 1) Verify the plugin package origin — confirm '@openguardrails/moltguard' refers to the official GitHub repo referenced in the SKILL.md (registry metadata lacked a homepage). 2) Understand privacy tradeoffs — the SKILL.md says detection is performed by a remote 'Core' service and that credentials and samples will be saved locally; expect inspected content to be sent to that service. 3) Review the plugin code (or the GitHub repo release) if possible before running the install command so you can confirm what data is transmitted and where. 4) If you need to limit exposure, consider running the plugin in a controlled environment first or backing up ~/.openclaw before installing so you can revert. 5) If you will claim agents across machines, ensure you trust the service and its billing/quota model before linking accounts.
